t:
(a) In General.—Paragraph (7) of section 6103(l) is amended by striking the last sentence thereof. 
    (b) Conforming Amendment.—Section 6103(l)(7)(D)(viii)(III) is amended by striking “sections 1710(a)(1)(I), 1710(a)(2), 1710(b), and 1712(a)(2)(B)” and inserting “sections 1710(a)(2)(G), 1710(a)(3), and 1710(b)”. 
    (c) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply to requests made after September 30, 2008.

fable.w: The section only makes technical amendments to section 6103(l)(7) by striking a sentence, updating cross-references, and setting an effective date. The word "requests" might suggest outside parties interacting with the government, but it refers to requests for disclosure of return information, not consultation, comment, hearing, or a right to sue over a federal decision. No outside party is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply to requests made after September 30, 2008.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Internal Revenue Code, specifically modifying cross-references and effective dates for tax information requests. It does not create any new process for public participation, consultation, or advisory input. The mention of 'requests' refers to statutory procedures for obtaining tax data, not to a participatory decision-making process involving outside parties.
qwen_block.s: (a) In General.—Paragraph (7) of section 6103(l) is amended by striking the last sentence thereof. (b) Conforming Amendment.—Section 6103(l)(7)(D)(viii)(III) is amended by striking “sections 1710(a)(1)(I), 1710(a)(2), 1710(b), and 1712(a)(2)(B)” and inserting “sections 1710(a)(2)(G), 1710(a)(3), and 1710(b)”. (c) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply to requests made after September 30, 2008.
qwen_block.b: Temptation: The text mentions "requests," which might imply a process where an outside party interacts with the government. However, these are requests for tax information under specific statutory provisions, not a participatory process in decision-making. The section is purely technical, amending cross-references and effective dates within the Internal Revenue Code. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, consultation, advisory boards, or hearings.

opus.w: The section only removes a sentence, updates statutory cross-references and sets an effective date for requests made after September 30, 2008. It does not set up a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders or right to sue. The word "requests" refers to disclosure requests under section 6103(l)(7), not to outside parties taking part in a federal decision. So this is not participation.
opus.s: Paragraph (7) of section 6103(l) is amended by striking the last sentence thereof.
opus.b:
**Step 1: The tempting reading.** The section mentions "requests" and amends section 6103(l)(7), which governs sharing tax return information with agencies that run needs-based programs. That could look like a formal exchange between the government and others. It fails the test because the section only removes a sentence, updates cross-references and sets an effective date. No one outside the federal government is consulted, invited to comment, given a hearing or given a right to sue before a federal decision.

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Internal Revenue Code, specifically striking and inserting section references and setting an effective date. It does not establish any process for public participation, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The actors involved are Congress (amending the law) and the IRS (implementing it), which are both inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending tax code sections related to information requests could implicitly affect how the public interacts with the IRS, but the text itself is purely technical legislative drafting (striking and inserting section numbers) with no mention of public comment, hearings, advisory committees, or consultation with outside parties.
